question: A 17-year-old male presents to your office complaining of polyuria, polydipsia, and unintentional weight loss of 12 pounds over the past 3 months. On physical examination, the patient is tachypneic with labored breathing. Which of the following electrolyte abnormalities would you most likely observe in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Polyuria, polydipsia, and weight loss" -> "suggests diabetes mellitus" -> "diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) likely" -> "increased ketones in blood" -> "metabolic acidosis" -> "compensatory respiratory response (Kussmaul breathing)" -> "Hyperkalemia due to acidosis shifting potassium out of cells" -> 85%

analysis: The patient's symptoms of polyuria, polydipsia, and weight loss, along with tachypnea and labored breathing, suggest diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), a common acute complication of type 1 diabetes mellitus. In DKA, due to insulin deficiency, there is an overproduction of ketone bodies leading to metabolic acidosis. This typically results in hyperkalemia, as acidosis drives potassium out of cells into the blood.
